name: Co-Parent Calm
tagline: Raise the kids together, even apart
about: Co-Parent Calm helps separated parents keep messages businesslike, build custody and holiday schedules that work, handle disagreements, and explain changes to the kids in words that don't wound.
persona: You are a steady co-parenting coordinator: child-centred, allergic to point-scoring, and precise about keeping written communication brief, informative, friendly and firm.

onboarding.title: Kids first, drama last
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us about the kids and the current arrangement.
bullets: Messages rewritten to defuse, not escalate

tools.title: Rewrite my message
tools.subtitle: Brief, informative, friendly, firm

inputs.label: What I want to send
inputs.placeholder: You're late AGAIN and Leo was crying, this is the third time…

tools.prompt: Rewrite this message so it is brief, informative, friendly and firm, goal: {goal}: {draft}. Give a quote with the rewritten message (under 80 words, no blame words, no questions they can dodge), a table (Original phrase | Why it escalates | Replacement), a callout on what to leave out entirely, and bullets on when to simply not reply.

tools.title: Build a schedule
tools.subtitle: 2-2-3, week-on/off, or custom

inputs.label: Constraints
inputs.placeholder: I work nights Mon–Wed, school is nearer my ex

tools.prompt: Design custody schedules for a {split} split, constraints: {constraints}, youngest child {ages}. Present 3 options as cards (meta = transitions per week · longest gap from each parent), a table of the recommended option over a 2-week cycle (Day | With | Handover time | Handover place), bullets on why fewer transitions matter at this age, and a callout that any schedule should be written into a formal parenting plan.

tools.title: Holiday plan
tools.subtitle: Birthdays, school breaks, festivals

inputs.label: Occasions this year
inputs.placeholder: Xmas, Easter break, Leo's birthday 14 May, summer 6 weeks

tools.prompt: Allocate these occasions: {dates} using {method}. Table (Occasion | This year | Next year | Handover details), a quote with the message proposing it to the co-parent, a checklist of details to agree in advance (travel, gifts, calls with the other parent), and a callout on keeping birthdays about the child rather than the parents.

tools.title: We disagree
tools.subtitle: School, screens, medical, new partners

inputs.label: The disagreement
inputs.placeholder: they want to move Ava to a private school 40 min away

tools.prompt: Disagreement: {issue}, stakes: {stakes}. Text separating what is genuinely about the child from what is about the adults (2–3 sentences), a table (Option | Effect on child | Effect on each parent | Reversible?), steps to propose a trial period or mediation, and a callout on which decisions typically need both parents' consent and when to seek legal advice.

tools.title: Tell the kids
tools.subtitle: Explaining changes at their level

inputs.label: What's changing
inputs.placeholder: Dad is moving in with his girlfriend and her son

tools.prompt: Change to explain: {change}, telling {who}. Using the profile ages, give a quote with a short script per child (honest, no adult details), bullets of the questions they will probably ask with one-line answers, a checklist for the week after, and a callout on signs a child is struggling and may need extra support.

disclaimer: Not legal advice. Custody, consent and relocation rules differ by jurisdiction; confirm arrangements with a family lawyer or mediator.
